newsitem.title: UK: Leeds shares slump after profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Leeds shares slump after profit warning.

text.p: Shares in Leeds Group Plc tumbled on Thursday after the textile company warned that conditions in the fashion sector had continued to deteriorate and profits for the current year were likely to below last year's level.
The stock was down 61-1/2p at 137-1/2 by 0934 GMT.
Chairman Robert Wade said its problems had been exacerbated by increasing imports of cheap clothing and by the continued depressed retail sector in France and Germany.
Wade said problems were concentrated in Leeds' Strines unit, where the company had responded by cutting jobs, and to a lesser extent in its fabric dyeing division.
Yet he said the company intended to maintain its final dividend.

The statement comes after Leeds warned in its first-half results in June that the fashion sector remained its most difficult market, and was vulnerable to volatile demand, weather extremes and rising imports.
